enlistment.title: Haredi men enlisted in the IDF, by draft year

rows.label: Haredi men reaching draft age each year

enlistment.question: Haredi men drafted into the IDF in each twelve-month period ending in July, from IDF data.
enlistment.source: IDF figures via Times of Israel
enlistment.note: The cohort row is the Jerusalem Post's estimate. IDI gives different figures for the same years: about 1,200 a year for most of the pre-war decade, 1,700 for 2023–24 and 2,940 for 2024–25 (https://en.idi.org.il/articles/61994). A different, much smaller measure is the response to draft orders: in the 2024 draft year, about 24,000 initial orders produced 798 enlistees (IDI, January 2026, https://en.idi.org.il/articles/63168)

reserve.title: Men aged 21–44 doing reserve service in an average month
reserve.question: Share of men aged 21–44 in reserve service in an average month, by self-defined religiosity.
reserve.source: Israel Democracy Institute (Finkelstein and Portal), from the CBS Labor Force Survey
reserve.note: "Religious" is the CBS self-definition, close to but not the same as national-religious. The figures are monthly rates, not headcounts

who-drafted.title: The most appropriate solution to drafting Haredim, November 2025
columns: Draft all except outstanding yeshiva students
Draft only those not really studying
who-drafted.question: "The most appropriate solution to the issue of drafting Haredim," asked after the end of the war.
who-drafted.note: IDI's label for the second group is "Arabs"; Druze are not reported separately in this result. About 75% of Haredi respondents chose the current system. IDI found the results "very similar" to September 2025
